newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares cheer up amid soft U.S. rate signals.
newsitem.headline: German shares cheer up amid soft U.S. rate signals.

text.p: German shares, having already proved themselves resilient in the face of Wall Street's tumble on Thursday, cheered up in afternoon trade on Friday as soft U.S price data eased rate hike worries.
The IBIS DAX index was up 19.61 points at 3,387.43 points at 1415 GMT, some 30 points ahead of the DAX index's mid-afternoon close at 3,359.29 points.
March DTB DAX futures were up 26 points at 3,395 points.
"We are clearly in a period of extreme volatility. We are going to have to get used to it," said one Frankfurt dealer, pointing out Friday's intraday low of just 3,321 DAX points.
But many dealers also said there were no major danger signals for the DAX at present.
"Think of it this way -- the dollar is in our favour and interest rates here are still relatively low," said another Frankfurt dealer.
"We don't have as much to worry about as the U.S. right now. There is still a lot of liquidity in this market and very few long term investors who want to sell," he added.
The afternoon rally boosted the market across the board, but the market was supported throughout the day by selective buying interest, mainly from domestic investors, dealers said.
Chemical shares rebounded from lows hit this week after disappointing news from Hoeschst AG that it did not plan to list its HMR unit.
And Daimler-Benz AG got a major boost after a well-received meeting with analysts at Goldman Sachs on Thursday and news of plan to set up a traffic navigation joint venture with Deutsche Telekom.
Daimler was up 2.85 marks at 130.80 marks in the afternoon.
Sports retailer Adidas AG also outperformed, continuing to profit from upgrades following its release of results earlier in the week.
Adidas was up more than five percent at 185.45 marks in afternoon trade, having earlier hit an all-time high of 189 marks.
Despite the solid performance relative to Wall Street, and the continued liquidity, dealers said the DAX would likely suffer more significant price swings in the week to come.
The afternoon's gains, coming at the end of a week of major rises and falls, leaves the IBIS DAX slightly below its closing level of 3,419.51 points a week ago.
"I think some investors, especially foreigners, are getting more and more nervous about the German market," said a dealer.

"These worries about EMU that are hitting the bond market aren't very good news for equities either," he said, referring to increasing speculation that Germany will not make the grade to launch the euro, and that monetary union may even have to be postponed.
That, dealers say, would be bad news for German equities, which have been widely expected to benefit from their future position at the heart of the euro zone.
German shares are also likely to be increasingly hit by the expiry of options next week on the DAX and its constituents -- a frequent cause of volatility on the market.

Dealers said the impact of the expiry was already affecting some prices on Friday. The strong gains on Allianz AG Holding, which rose 41 marks to 3,384 marks in bourse trade, appeared to be connected with the options market.

Elsewhere, engineering company Mannesmann AG pared most of their losses on Friday, first dropping sharply on talk of an earnings downgrade by a major bank, but then recovering after the company released an outlook for higher 1997 earnings.
The shares were trading down 6.45 marks at 640 marks in afternoon trade, well off a low of 614 marks.
--Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525
